Ellipsis of dès potron-minet, of uncertain origin. The original locution [1640] was dès le poitron-jacquet (“from dawn”). It was composed of Old French poitron, from the posterio (“hindquarters", "ass"”) (compare English posterior), accompanied by jacquet, the name of the squirrel, literally meaning "as soon as you see the squirrel's backside peeking out". The term evolved to potron-jacquet or potron-jaquet and finally to potron-minet by substitution of jacquet with minet ("cat"). The Burgundian term pauitrou-jaiquai or potrou jacquet also referred to early morning, from the grazing jacquet.…
